analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר. The words that follow are God's direct speech, beginning with יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם, “Let the waters be gathered.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: The singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר (“he said”) identifies אֱלֹהִים as the one speaker who commands the waters to gather and the dry land to appear.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: God commands the waters to be gathered אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד (into one place) so that dry land may appear. The destination establishes the sense of physical gathering.
analysis.morphology: Niphal jussive, third person masculine plural, agreeing with הַמַּיִם (the waters).

analysis.evidence: מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם locates the waters beneath the heavens. The prefix מִן marks the place from which they are to gather, and אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד gives their destination.
analysis.morphology: Preposition תַּחַת with prefixed מִן. The נ assimilates to the initial ת, yielding מִתַּחַת.

analysis.evidence: מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם locates the waters beneath the sky. God commands them to gather in one place so that dry land appears.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + masculine plural absolute noun

analysis.evidence: In יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם … אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד, אֶל introduces the destination of the waters as they gather, “to one place.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד means “into one place,” specifying where the waters are to gather. The masculine singular אֶחָד agrees with מָקוֹם and supplies the meaning “one.”
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד, “to one place,” אֶחָד agrees with מָקוֹם and specifies a single place where the waters are to gather.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine singular absolute, modifying מָקוֹם.

analysis.evidence: וְתֵרָאֶה agrees with its feminine singular subject הַיַּבָּשָׁה, “the dry land.” It continues the command יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם, “let the waters gather,” so that the dry land becomes visible.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ + Niphal imperfect, third person feminine singular, with jussive force.

analysis.evidence: God commands the waters to gather in one place. הַיַּבָּשָׁה is the subject of the feminine singular verb וְתֵרָאֶה, “let it appear,” and denotes the ground exposed as the waters gather.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי כֵן, כֵן means “so” and refers back to both parts of the command. וַיְהִי reports that the waters gathered and the dry land appeared as commanded.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי כֵן, “and it was so,” כֵן refers back to God’s command that the waters gather in one place and the dry land appear. The phrase affirms that both happened as commanded.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb with no prefix or suffix.
